avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Induces intestinal transporters (P-gp, BCRP) and may reduce sofosbuvir bioavailability; potential loss of antiviral efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue St. John's Wort at least 2 weeks before and during sofosbuvir therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin-containing supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong inducer of drug transporters and metabolism; significantly reduces sofosbuvir plasma concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; contact prescriber if tuberculosis treatment required

caution_supplements.name: High-dose Antioxidants (Vitamin E, Vitamin C)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May theoretically interfere with viral suppression; limited evidence but caution warranted
caution_supplements.action: Use moderate doses; avoid megadose supplementation during therapy

caution_supplements.name: Milk Thistle
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild P-glycoprotein modulation; potential minor effect on absorption
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for reduced efficacy; separate dosing by 2+ hours if used

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase sofosbuvir absorption but clinical significance is minimal; some formulations are food-independent
caution_foods.action: Take with or without food per product labeling; consistency recommended

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: May inhibit intestinal transporters (P-gp); potential modest increase in sofosbuvir levels
caution_foods.action: Avoid excessive grapefruit juice consumption; not an absolute contraindication

monitoring_notes: Sofosbuvir has minimal hepatic metabolism and low drug-drug interaction potential, making it relatively safe with supplements. Primary monitoring should focus on renal function (creatinine clearance) and confirmation of viral response, as transporter inhibition or induction may affect bioavailability in renal-impaired patients.
